description: I'm an Integrated Biology student passionate about science, space exploration, environmental research, and emerging technologies. I enjoy scientific research, creative thinking, and exploring innovative solutions to real-world challenges. I'm particularly interested in astronaut health monitoring and the intersection of biology and technology.
summary:
ASTROSYNTRA is a working web application that helps researchers understand how an astronaut's biological state changes during long-duration spaceflight — not by watching each health metric separately, but by studying how physiological, behavioural and environmental signals change together in the context of the mission.

The app analyses 45 days of simulated data for three fictional astronauts, each compared against their own personal baseline. Its signature Bio-Constellation maps which body systems co-vary; a Temporal Relationship Explorer tests whether changes lead or follow each other; and every finding opens an Evidence Trace showing the raw data, method and uncertainty. A Mission Scenario Simulator, nine-detector Data Quality Observatory, Circadian Explorer, countermeasure analysis and crew-level human-factors view complete the toolkit. A Research Bridge connects to NASA's real Open Science Data Repository — 647 studies — with offline fallback.

Because crews on lunar and Mars missions can't rely on Earth, ASTROSYNTRA runs entirely offline and never claims causation or medical diagnosis — it makes complex data honest, explainable and explorable.
details:
What it does and how it works

ASTROSYNTRA is a fully functional web application — a "biological research observatory" for long-duration space missions, not a mock-up. Given daily health records, it builds a personal baseline from each astronaut's first 14 days, detects periods where several indicators shift together, groups them into cross-system patterns with statistical associations, and presents everything through interactive scientific instruments:

  • Bio-Constellation — a network of biological systems; a link appears only where 12+ paired days support it, and unmeasured systems are honestly shown as "no data"
  • Temporal Relationship Explorer — lagged correlation (±10 days) with confidence intervals, sample sizes and multiple-comparison correction, state saved in shareable links
  • Evidence Trace — every observation is reproducible from the raw records, parameters and engine version
  • Mission Scenario Simulator, Data Quality Observatory (9 detectors), Circadian & Light Explorer, Countermeasure Research, Immune & Microbiome layer, privacy-first Crew Human-Factors view, and Deep-Space offline mode

A Space Biology Research Bridge connects live to NASA's Open Science Data Repository (647 real studies via its documented API, with organism labelling and an offline snapshot fallback).

Benefits and intended impact

It shifts crew health review from isolated alarms to one connected, explainable picture — with honest uncertainty, so findings can be trusted and debated. Designed for missions where a link to Earth isn't guaranteed, it runs 100% locally.

Tools used

React 19, strict TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, native SVG visualisation, Vitest (48 tests passing), IndexedDB. No paid AI APIs. Demo video produced with Playwright + ffmpeg.

How it's creative

The core idea is relational — biological relationships in mission context, not another dashboard. The ORBITAL ATLAS design system makes it feel like a scientific instrument, and every result carries its receipts.

Factors we considered

Scientific integrity above all: never correlation-as-causation, no imputed data, every record labelled measured/self-reported/simulated, no diagnoses or invented thresholds. Also privacy (aggregated crew view only), accessibility, offline operation, and reproducibility.
